notes: Interim final rule amending 38 CFR 4.10 to state that ameliorative effects of medication should not be estimated or discounted when evaluating functional impairment at examination, responding to Ingram v. Collins, 38 Vet. App. 130 (2025). Rescinded ten days after its effective date.

notes: Final rule rescinding the interim final rule published 2026-02-17 (91 FR 7118) and restoring the prior regulatory text of 38 CFR 4.10, effective immediately upon publication.

manualLifecycleOverride.reason: VA rescinded the interim final rule ten days after it took effect, restoring the prior text of 38 CFR 4.10. The rescission document 2026-03940 (91 FR 9712) itself remains operative law, so a documents-only lifecycle derivation would show 'effective'; the RIN's rulemaking outcome is recorded as rescinded so the application does not treat the brief 2026-02-17 through 2026-02-27 medication-interpretation rule as current authority.

impact.summary: Interim final rule that would have directed examiners and adjudicators not to estimate or discount the ameliorative effects of medication when evaluating functional impairment under 38 CFR 4.10, with potential reach across the rating schedule; VA rescinded it on 2026-02-27 and restored the prior regulatory text, so the pre-rescission section 4.10 interpretation (including the Ingram v. Collins, 38 Vet. App. 130 (2025) line of cases) governs as of 2026-09-01. Retained in the registry because rating-examination handling of medication effects is relevant to how condition severity is evaluated across secondary-condition mappings.
